How I got here

My route into software started with a simple habit: taking an idea apart until I understood how it worked. Computer Science at the University of Dar es Salaam gave that curiosity a foundation. Building real products taught me the rest: how to connect an interface to an API, untangle a backend, and turn a promising idea into something people can actually use.

Today I'm based in Dar es Salaam, working with founders and teams across agriculture, commerce, property, and legal technology. I co-founded Ecofy Africa and work across its frontend, backend, and AI. Elsewhere, my work has helped shape products including GloboExpats, Habitek, and Wakili Msomi, alongside backend systems for Osher Market, Falco, and TanStack Tanzania.

Where I stand

I work across frontend, mobile, backend, and applied AI, moving comfortably between the interface and the systems behind it. That range has taken me from community marketplaces and property platforms to legal assistants and internal management tools. My role changes with the project; the standard stays the same: understand the problem, make thoughtful decisions, and build something that holds together.

As chairperson of the UDSM 3D Solutions & Robotics Lab, I learned to bring people, ideas, and technical work into the same room. Our projects included Nena AI and TanStack Tanzania. I bring that same approach to client work today: collaborate closely, take ownership of my contribution, and care about the details that make a product feel finished.
